source_text: Die quo in neruo mansimus ostensum est mihi hoc. Uideo locum illum quem retro uideram, et Dinocraten mundo corpore, bene uestitum, refrigerantem; et ubi erat uulnus, uideo cicatricem: et piscina illa summisso margine usque ad umbilicum pueri; et aquam de ea trahebat sine cessatione. Et super marginem fiala aurea plena aqua; et accessit Dinocrates et de ea bibere coepit; quae fiala non deficiebat. Et satiatus accessit ludere de aqua more infantium gaudens. Et experrecta sum. Et intellexi translatum eum esse de poena.
pass_a_gloss: On the day on which we stayed in the stocks this was shown to me. I see that place which I had seen before, and Dinocrates with a clean body, well clothed, taking refreshment; and where the sore had been, I see a scar; and that pool with its rim lowered to the boy's navel; and he was drawing water from it without stopping. And on the rim a golden bowl full of water; and Dinocrates came up and began to drink from it; and that bowl did not run out. And having had enough he went away to play with the water, rejoicing in the way of little children. And I woke up. And I understood that he had been carried across out of punishment.
pass_b_english: On the day we spent in the stocks, this was shown to me. I saw the same place I had seen before, and Dinocrates there with his body clean, well dressed, and at rest. Where his wound had been I now saw a scar, and the pool stood with its rim lowered to the boy's navel, and he was drawing water from it without ceasing. Upon the rim stood a golden bowl full of water, and Dinocrates stepped up and began to drink from it, and the bowl did not fail.
Then, satisfied, he stepped back to sport with the water, joyous as young children are. And I awoke, and I understood that he had been brought out of his punishment.
